description: The plot titled “Massive Activation of baseline” illustrates how the maximum activation value varies across model layers for four signals: attn_output, attn_residual, ffn_output, and ffn_residual. The x-axis is labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately layers 0 to 23 with major ticks shown at 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20. The y-axis is labeled “Max Activation Value,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0 up to about 1600 with evenly spaced tick marks at roughly 200-unit intervals. The attn_output line is blue with a dashed style and no markers; it stays near 0 for most layers and then rises late, reaching roughly ~250 by the final layer. The attn_residual line is orange with a dotted style and no markers; it is near 0 through about layer 4, jumps sharply to around ~1400 at about layer 6, remains near ~1500–1600 through roughly layers 14–21, and then drops steeply near the end to around ~250 at the final layer. The ffn_output line is green with a dash-dot style and no markers; it is near 0 early, shows a sharp spike around layer 5 to roughly ~1400, returns close to 0 by around layers 8–12, spikes again around layer 13 to roughly ~800, stays low afterward, and then shows another late spike near layer 22 to roughly ~1200 before dropping again by the final layer. The ffn_residual line is red with a solid style and no markers; it is near 0 through about layer 4, jumps to around ~1400 at about layer 5, increases to about ~1500 by around layer 7, stays near ~1500–1600 through roughly layers 14–21, then drops sharply near layer 22 to around ~400 and ends around ~600 at the final layer.
